claim: An accepted, non-conflicted typed policy suggestion can replace exactly its live review card with one linked review policy block only against the exact unchanged semantic draft.
verified: Suggestion creation stores a deterministic semantic policy-content fingerprint that excludes suggestion review-card markers
Application requires the exact suggestion, proposal event, accepted decision event, and current editor revision
Pending, rejected, conflicted, missing, or invalid suggestion state cannot mutate the policy draft
Any semantic policy-content change since proposal creation rejects application before editor mutation
The suggestion marker must occur exactly once and its stable identity must not collide with an existing policy block
The accepted proposal becomes one review-status policy block whose stable policy ID is the suggestion ID
The existing editor controller rechecks the revision during replacement and stops a simulated preparation/replacement race
A real Lexical integration test confirms the card node is removed and one exact PolicyBlockNode is created
The product separates Accept from Apply to draft and explains the unchanged-content guard
Production TypeScript and Vite build passes
limitations: Reviewer identity is installation-provided and is not authenticated.
No packaged two-client interaction or disconnected apply/conflict resolution is included in this proof.
MCP can inspect suggestion decisions but cannot apply an accepted suggestion through this product-only route.
The action applies the complete proposal as one review policy block; partial edit and semantic-quality validation remain open.
A conflicting offline rejection that has not yet arrived cannot be predicted; once present, conflicted state blocks application.
